context:
Goal: every guard that runs protects work you actually do, with one home per guard.
Problem (rule): banchi keeps Codex halves of four guards (shared-tree, silent-write, kill-by-name, and their tokenizer); claude-settings ships no Codex hooks, so these have no shared home and drift from the Claude Code copies.
Based on (read): plan, banchi rows 1, 7, 8, 9: the Codex half has no cs runner (banchi D135); the tokenizer has drifted from hooks/guard_core.py.
Based on (incident): banchi 2026-09-06 checkout lost about 240 lines; 2026-09-09 and 09-10 pkill -f hit port 8000 (rows 1, 8), caught today by the Claude Code copies.
Departs from: banchi main, which keeps the Codex halves — option a deletes them, option b adds Codex hooks to claude-settings.

options.gain: One home per guard; no drifting copy.
options.how: A banchi lane deletes the Codex-only parts of rows 1, 7, 8 and the tokenizer (row 9); the Claude Code guards stay in claude-settings.
options.label: Delete the Codex halves
options.lose: A Codex session in banchi runs with no guard.

options.gain: Codex sessions get the same guards in every repo.
options.how: claude-settings ships Codex hooks that call the shared guards; banchi then deletes its copies.
options.label: Port to claude-settings
options.lose: A new Codex runner to build and keep.

options.label: Keep in banchi
options.lose: The copies keep drifting from the shared guards.

title: banchi's guards that run only under Codex: delete them, or port them to claude-settings?
why: Sessions run in Claude Code; a guard copy for a tool you do not use only drifts.
